25: MARYA [rises indignantly]. No, that's too much—Such rudeness, such impertinence.
24: MARYA [looking through the window]. What is that? It looked as if something had flown by. Was it a magpie or some other bird? KHLESTAKOV [kisses her shoulder and looks through the window]. It's a magpie.
22: KHLESTAKOV [moving nearer]. It only seems near to you. Imagine it's far. How happy I would be, mademoiselle, if I could clasp you in my embrace.
20: KHLESTAKOV [moving nearer]. Why far? It's all the same if it's near.
19: KHLESTAKOV. Why do you move your chair away? It is better for us to sit near each other. MARYA [moving away]. Why near? It's all the same if it's far away.
17: MARYA. Love? I don't understand love. I never knew what love is. [Moves her chair away.]
14: KHLESTAKOV. What's the use? I know them anyway.
13: MARYA. Well, tell me. What verses will you write for me?
12: KHLESTAKOV. Oh, what are verses! I know a lot of them.
11: MARYA. Any at all. Pretty, new verses.
10: MARYA. You are just saying that—I should like to ask you—I'd rather you would write some verses in my album for a souvenir. You must know very many. KHLESTAKOV. Anything you desire, mademoiselle. Ask! What verses will you have?
8: KHLESTAKOV. Your lips, mademoiselle, are better than any weather.
6: MARYA. I haven't the least idea what you are talking about—scarf!—Peculiar weather today, isn't it?
4: KHLESTAKOV. Oh, mademoiselle, how I long to be your scarf, so that I might embrace your lily neck.
2: MARYA. You are making fun of me. You're only ridiculing the provincials.
0: KHLESTAKOV. What a beautiful scarf that is.
